name: Cloudflare Browser Run / Kitesurf

modes.label: Chromium Browser Sessions
modes.note: Plus monthly-average daily-peak concurrency fee; monthly runtime total rounded to nearest hour.

modes.label: Quick Actions
modes.note: Stateless API actions; no concurrency-fee meter; not a long-lived session.

modes.label: Kitesurf beta
modes.note: Free while beta; stateless Workers-native engine; not full Chrome or long authenticated sessions.

plans.name: Workers Free
plans.note: Chromium is available on Workers Free but capped at 10 browser-minutes/day (429 until the next UTC day), 3 concurrent browsers, a new browser every 20 s and 1 Quick Actions request per 10 s; sizes_allowed is kept to Kitesurf beta because ~5 h/month cannot carry a real workload. Kitesurf beta account limits apply. No published CPU/RAM size.

plans.name: Workers Paid
plans.note: 10 included browser-hours/month, valued at $.09/hour. Ten averaged concurrent browsers included; each additional averaged browser costs $2/month. Workers requests and CPU may add charges.

features.ip_note: All traffic egresses from Cloudflare IP ranges; no per-request IP rotation; always identified as bot traffic (non-removable cf-biso-* and Web Bot Auth Signature headers). No third-party proxy option is documented; Outbound Workers can route selected http:// (not https://) hostnames through your own Worker. An optional `location` (ISO country code) session option exists in the Workers binding.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
Concurrency fees use the monthly average of daily peak concurrency, not the monthly maximum or a time-weighted average. Add this fee outside the current engine.
Browser usage is metered in seconds and the monthly sum is rounded to the nearest hour. Do not impose a one-hour minimum on each start.
The paid technical concurrency cap is 200; the billing allowance is only 10 averaged browsers. Keep-alive limits concern inactivity, not maximum active session length.
Kitesurf is a beta, stateless alternative without full Chromium graphics, video, WebGL or long-lived authenticated state. Its zero price is not a free general-purpose computer.
Worker requests/CPU, inference, recording storage and other unpriced charges remain separate. No browser CPU/RAM allocation guarantee was found.

Idle tail is billed: a session not closed with browser.close() keeps consuming browser time until the inactivity timeout (60 s default, up to 10 min via keep_alive per the limits page; the Workers binding reference allows keepAlive 10 s to 20 min). Sessions also close when Browser Run rolls out a new release.
Session recordings are retained 30 days then deleted; no recording storage price is published.

fleet.tiers: Workers Free 3; Workers Paid 200 default. Beyond 200 submit limit-increase request for review.
fleet.notes: Browser Sessions quota, not Browser Run HTTP-request rate. Paid plan includes only 10 averaged browsers in price, not a cap of 10. 10/50 fit paid quota; 300/1,000 need approved increase. Free creates 1/20 seconds; paid 3/second. No human-review turnaround stated. Quick Actions request rate: Workers Free 1 per 10 s, Workers Paid 30/s. Workers Free /crawl: 5 jobs/day, max 100 pages per crawl. Workers Paid defaults were raised on 2026-08-20 (concurrent browsers 120->200, new browsers/s 1->3, Quick Actions req/s 10->30); published limits are defaults, not maximums.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

extras.item: Workers usage when driving Browser Run from a Worker
extras.price: Workers Paid: 10M requests/month included then $0.30/M; 30M CPU-ms included then $0.02/M CPU-ms

snapshot_auto.quote: For Puppeteer, Playwright, and CDP, no caching is used. Content exists only in memory for the duration of the rendering operation and is discarded immediately after the response is returned.
snapshot_auto.note: Sessions close on idle (keep_alive 60 s default, max 10 min) and nothing is saved. Kitesurf is explicitly 'stateless'. Only opt-in session recordings (DOM/input events, 30 days) survive, which are replay logs, not restorable state.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Cloudflare processes content ephemerally and does not retain customer-submitted HTML or generated output (such as PDFs or screenshots) beyond what is required to perform the rendering operation.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No browser-state checkpoint or persistent profile API. Docs show DIY cookie/localStorage persistence: Playwright storageState saved to KV by your code (playwright page). The '/snapshot' Quick Action returns page content+screenshot, not a restorable snapshot.

egress_allowlist.quote: Guardrails limit a Browser Run session's HTTP and HTTPS requests to permitted hostnames.
egress_allowlist.note: allowedDomains (<=50, one wildcard each) + allowedDomainSets (<=4: Cloudflare 'common-cdns' or your hosted HTTPS list); empty allowedDomains blocks all web requests. Fixed at session start. Blocked requests get 403 cf-mitigated: guardrails. Not for Quick Actions, not supported with Kitesurf. Hostnames only, no IP/CIDR rules.

guest_firewall.note: No shell or OS access to the browser host: control is CDP/Puppeteer/Playwright only, so you cannot run nftables/iptables.
